scope: Static comparison of the signed wrapper and source adapters, with direct inspection of the retained exact price, partial admission, precision, and catalogue assembly engines. This is not a substitute for their complete execution receipts.
findings: The old full signed invoice is reconstructed from PR7480 WORD.json.gz and asserted equal to the frozen PR7480 RESULT.json price.after. It is not substituted with the PR7334 or 18-stage ingredient invoice.
The old and candidate native inventories are recomputed, required to have no bad inputs, and matched against their respective hash-bound native receipts.
The full 17-stage caller has an explicit byte digest and must be reproduced byte identically by the source emitters.
The two local invoice adaptations are identical to source price.py and require each old text to occur exactly once. The remaining adaptations call the unmodified source adapt.py.
The source adapter removes stale native and precision reuse. It recomputes the candidate common grid and native envelope, then requires equality with the new native receipt.

The source price gate recomputes both directed crossing engines, requires the candidate crossing above the old upper bound, and requires both old-price engines to reject the new claim. Its conservative claim and strictly larger tested point both lie below the new crossing.

The repeated partial-admission gate computes the complete invoice, all ordinary scalar and conversion charges, and all 54 strict plus four functional outer predicates. The wrapper requires exact equality of this invoice and gate with the primary price record.

The catalogue assembler requires contiguous full coverage, source word digests, absolute-phase rejection controls, 17 native occurrences, invoice-matched paid and productive counts, matching caller hashes, and the fixed precision/tape bounds.
No relaxation, omitted caller stage, stale source native, or optimistic price substitution was found.
